extracted.intended_audience: creative writers (poets, fiction & nonfiction authors) seeking publication in literary magazines, presses, and anthologies
extracted.subtask_short: submitting creative writing to lit journals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writers on how to prepare and submit creative work (poetry, fiction, nonfiction, art, chapbooks) to literary magazines, presses, calendars, and anthologies. Covers eligibility, formats, themes, deadlines, fees, and editorial preferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted genres
rubrics_metrics.description: Which genres the venue accepts (poetry, fiction, essays, book reviews, art, photography, creative nonfiction, flash fiction, CNF, chapbooks, artwork, comics).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples from page: Able Muse: "poetry, fiction, essays, book reviews, art, and photography"; The Pensieve: "fiction, creative nonfiction, and poetry"; SPANK the CARP: "flash fiction, short stories, CNF, and poetry, including shape poetry"; Palooka: "prose, art, photography, comics, and chapbooks." Use each venue's listed genres to decide where to submit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission deadlines and reading periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific deadline dates or open reading windows (single-date deadlines, seasonal windows, rolling/year‑round reading).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Able Muse: "Deadline: July 15, 2026" and "Submission opens yearly January 1 and closes July 15"; Fifth Stanza Press: "open reading period... May 1 through July 31, 2026"; many listings are "Year-round" or "Rolling." Check each listing for exact close dates and whether there are earlier/member windows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length and format limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Maximum (and sometimes minimum) word counts, page counts, and format expectations for individual pieces or manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: "Essays should not exceed 4000 words" (anthology); "short stories of less than 5,000 words" (Mountain Jay Books); "creative nonfiction and fiction of up to 3,000 words" (Kings River Review); Magazine1 flash contest: "500 word limit"; Split Rock Press chapbooks: "15–30 pages." Follow each venue's specific numeric limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of pieces per submission
rubrics_metrics.description: How many poems/artwork/works you may include in a single submission package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Red Shoe Press (Oregon Poetry Calendar): "Submit 1-5 poems in a single Word document"; Kings River Review: "up to 5 pieces of artwork and photography... and up to 5 poems." Observe per-venue piece-count limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission method and file requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: How to send work (Submittable, email, web form), permitted file formats (.doc, .docx, .jpeg, pasted body text), and prohibitions (no attachments, no email submissions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: many use Submittable links (e.g., bluemountainreview.submittable.com); New Verse News: "paste your non-simultaneous submission and a brief bio in the text of an email (no attachments, please)"; Red Shoe Press: "No email submissions." Artwork: "send as .JPEG files." Also follow instructions such as "Submit at www..." and venue-specific file-type requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blind submissions / anonymity
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether submissions must be anonymized (no identifying info inside the submitted file) or whether the venue reads anonymously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Cæsura: "All work must be submitted blind (no identifying information in the file)." Palooka: "read anonymously." If a venue requires blind files, remove names/headers from manuscripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simultaneous submissions policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether venues allow simultaneous submissions (submitting the same piece to multiple outlets) or require exclusivity / non-simultaneous submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Cæsura: "Simultaneous submissions are welcome." The New Verse News: asks for a "non-simultaneous submission." Check each listing for whether simultaneous submissions are acceptable and whether they require notification/withdrawal upon acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Previously unpublished vs previously published
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether a venue requires previously unpublished work, permits previously published work, or makes exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: The Pensieve: "We are looking for previously unpublished pieces"; Red Shoe Press (poetry calendar): "Previously published and simultaneous submissions are okay." Note each venue's position on prior publication and whether online/website appearances count as publication (Mountain Jay Books excludes personal websites from 'previously published').

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility and targeted contributors
rubrics_metrics.description: Special eligibility criteria based on career stage, student status, age, or other target demographics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: The Pensieve: seeks "emerging writers, such as students, amateurs, and professionals... at the beginning of their careers"; Fifth Stanza Press: publishes "debut and second collections of poetry by writers in midlife or later"; Kings River Review: "current 2-year community college students." Follow venue-specific eligibility rules before submitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic or institutional restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Limits based on residence, region, or institutional affiliation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Gold Man Review: "we only accept submissions from writers in Oregon, Alaska, Hawaii, California, and Washington"; Red Shoe Press calendar: "Work accepted only from poets currently living in Oregon." Verify residency or institutional limits where specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theme or prompt requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the issue/anthology has a theme or prompt that submissions must address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Cæsura 2026 theme: "LIFELINE"; Magazine1 summer issue theme: "heat"; Thorn & Bloom: "The Body As Archive." Anthology calls may ask for pieces addressing a specific question or emotional prompt (e.g., "What are the conversations you most wanted to have..."). Submit work that engages the stated theme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership, early windows, and member-specific rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether members receive earlier deadlines or special submission windows or different rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Cæsura: accepts submissions through June 1st, "June 15 for members of Poetry Center San Jose!" Check whether your membership grants access to earlier deadlines or special categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response time, notification schedule, and publication timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimated response dates and publication timelines provided by the venue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Fifth Stanza Press: "All poets will receive a response by the end of October... selected manuscript will be announced in the fall and published in early 2027." Red Shoe Press: "Responses by July 2026, publication by August 2026." Use these timelines to plan simultaneous submissions and follow-ups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment, contributor copies, honorarium, and rights/rights reversion
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether authors receive payment, contributor copies, honoraria, and how rights are handled after publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Fifth Stanza Press: selected poet "will receive author copies and an honorarium"; Split Rock Press (selected authors) receive "20 contributor copies and a 50% discount on additional copies"; Red Shoe Press: "Upon publication, all rights revert back to poet." Check each venue's payment and rights language before agreeing to publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reading/submission fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the venue charges a reading or submission fee and the fee amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Split Rock Press: "There is a $12 reading fee." Other listings specify "No submission fee" or do not charge. Confirm fees on the venue's submission page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial preferences and desired qualities
rubrics_metrics.description: Descriptive criteria editors use to judge work (voice, craft, originality, immersive quality, boundary-pushing, not pretentious, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phrases on page indicating editorial taste: The Pensieve: seeks work "compelling, beautifully written, and immersive—transporting readers into a world of the author’s creation"; Gold Man Review: "we love writing that pushes boundaries"; SPANK the CARP: "thought-provoking, sophisticated, yet not pretentious or obscure"; Palooka: "Bold voices. Brave stories." Tailor submissions to match the venue's stated aesthetic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artwork and visual submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific technical and artistic requirements for visual submissions (file type, subject matter, artistic standard).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Kings River Review: "artwork and photography sent as .JPEG files"; SPANK the CARP: accepts images and photos that depict Carp and Koi "and have a strong artistic element." Follow size, format, and thematic guidance provided by the venue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions and special prohibitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit 'do not' rules such as 'no email submissions', 'no attachments', or content restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Red Shoe Press: "No email submissions." New Verse News: "no attachments, please." Venues may also define content limits (e.g., previously published allowed or disallowed). Read submission pages for prohibitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection process notes (judges, guest editors, or editorial decision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Information about how work is selected (named judges, guest editors, or editorial boards) or announcements about judged contests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Magazine1 notes a flash prose contest with judge "Aimee Nezukumatathil." Other listings indicate editorial selection or announce timelines for judge decisions. If judge or contest status is specified, it may affect submission strategy.
